jobs.title: Associate or Full Professor of Environmental Science and Policy and Program Director, Tenured, Augus
jobs.description:
Description

Chapman University invites applications for an Associate or Full Professor of Environmental Science & Policy and Program Director in the Schmid College of Science and Technology starting August 2027. This is a full-time, tenured position that requires work to be performed in the State of California with specific in-person teaching responsibilities and required on-campus availability at Chapman's Orange campus.

Chapman University is a nationally ranked R2 institution offering traditional undergraduate and graduate programs in the heart of Orange County, one of Southern California's most diverse and vibrant regions. Our faculty are academic leaders who excel in both research and teaching. Dedicated to forward-looking, personalized education, we create an environment for unlimited achievement by both our students and faculty. More information about Chapman University is available at www.chapman.edu.

The Environmental Science & Policy Program is uniquely seated within two colleges at Chapman University: the Schmid College of Science and Technology and the Wilkinson College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences. Schmid and Wilkinson Colleges embody Chapman's mission of providing students with personalized educational experiences by fostering an outstanding community of teacher-scholars across a broad range of undergraduate and graduate programs. Schmid College has a new 140,000 sq ft home, the Keck Center for Science and Engineering. More information about Schmid and Wilkinson Colleges is available at www.chapman.edu/science
and www.chapman.edu/wilkinson
, respectively.

The undergraduate-only serving Environmental Science & Policy Program is home to a diverse group of faculty with interdisciplinary specializations across the breadth of environmental sciences (ecology, engineering, hydrology, remote sensing) and environmental studies (anthropology, environmental justice, natural resource governance, political science, sociology). The program serves the interdisciplinary Environmental Science & Policy B.S. degree, the Environmental Science minor, and the Environmental Studies minor.

We seek candidates with an active research program in areas including but not limited to:

Environmental health
Environmental toxicology
Water, soil, and/or air quality
Environmental contaminants
Natural resource governance

We value candidates who can identify avenues for collaboration both within and outside of the institution.

Faculty Role Responsibilities

The successful candidate will teach lower- and upper-level courses that contribute to the major and minors within the Environmental Science & Policy Program, maintain an active research program, and advise/mentor undergraduate research students. Significant scholarship, including publishing in peer-reviewed journals, presenting at relevant research conferences, and obtaining and managing extramural grants is an expectation of the position.

Required Responsibilities Include:

Teach lower- and upper-division Environmental Science & Policy courses, including core and elective courses. Current course descriptions are available at https://catalog.chapman.edu.
Continue a research program in interdisciplinary environmental sciences, including publishing papers and presenting work in this area at local and national conferences.
Actively contribute as an integral member of the Schmid College of Science and Technology in the ongoing development, implementation, and assessment of their academic and degree programs.
Perform service to the unit, college, university, profession, and wider community as expected of a tenured faculty member.

Program Director Responsibilities

The successful candidate will lead the Environmental Science & Policy faculty and degree program as Program Director for a minimum of three years in an at-will, compensated appointment separate from their faculty role.

Required Responsibilities Include:

Provide leadership, vision, and a voice for affiliated faculty, students, and degree programs.
Oversee program budget and advocate on behalf of the program for resource use.
Lead curriculum alignment and revisions, assessment reports, and course scheduling for the program.
Coordinate and participate in program and college events, including events for student recruitment and commencement, as appropriate.
Assign faculty to courses and hire appropriate part-time lecturers where needed.
Facilitate communication and collaboration between Schmid and Wilkinson Colleges pertaining to the support of this interdisciplinary program.

Qualifications

An earned Ph.D. in one of the environmental sciences (e.g., Biology, Chemistry, Environmental Science & Management) or related field by the start of employment from an accredited institution.
Earned tenure at the current institution of employment or equivalent.
A strong history of interdisciplinary environmental science research, including evidence of an independent, nationally recognized, externally funded research program.
Evidence of effective teaching at the undergraduate level, particularly in experiential learning courses, such as a senior capstone course, or upper division coursework.
Experience in curriculum development and learning outcome assessment.
Experience in leadership or administrative roles in academic service settings, such as college governance, curriculum, or assessment committees, ideally connected to interdisciplinary endeavors.

Application Instructions

Qualified Candidates Should Submit The Following Electronically Via Interfolio:

Cover letter detailing qualifications related to the position description.
Curriculum Vitae.
Statement of teaching philosophy that includes a brief description of past teaching experience, no more than two pages.
Research Statement that details current and future environmental science research, no more than two pages.
Statement of leadership philosophy that includes a brief description of administrative and leadership experiences as they relate to Program Director-level service, no more than one page.
Contact information for three professional references. Letters will be requested from short-listed candidates.

Inquiries may be directed to Richelle Tanner, Search Committee Chair, at schmidcollege@chapman.edu. Please use "Environmental Science & Policy Faculty Position" as the email subject line.

Application review will begin October 11, 2026, and will continue until the position is filled. This position is subject to final budget approval. Salary range for this position is $105,000 - $125,000. Successful completion of a background check is required for the final candidate.

jobs.description:
Job Description

At GHD, we don’t just believe in the power of commitment, we live and breathe it every day.

That’s why we pledge to empower all of our people to make a positive impact. Combining our deep technical expertise with the capabilities of our clients and partners, we respond to some of the most complex challenges facing our planet today.

See where your commitment could take you.

Our pledge to you

Join GHD

That’s the #PowerOfCommittment

There’s no pledge more important than the one we make to look after our environment, and we’re committed to helping you do exactly that.

Join us as we strive to ensure a sustainable future for our communities and the world we live in.

Become part of our global network of skilled engineers, scientists, auditors, planners and environmental specialists, all working together to leave this world better than we found it.

Are you ready to lead a dynamic team of Emergency Response/Preparedness and environmental professionals in tackling some of the most pressing challenges facing our environment today?

Who are we looking for?

As a Project Manager
at GHD, you will not only mentor and guide the team but also take the reins in environmental emergencies, collaborating closely with clients and agencies to ensure effective response and resolution.

Your role will extend beyond project management to include business development and client expansion activities, where your expertise in environmental engineering, geology, or related fields will shine. With 5+ years of project management experience under your belt, including a proven track record in emergency response, client relationship management, and business development, you'll bring a wealth of knowledge to the table.

From conducting environmental sampling and monitoring to spearheading regional visibility initiatives, your passion for environmental stewardship and problem-solving will drive our success. If you thrive in a fast-paced environment, possess exceptional communication skills, and are committed to making a difference, join us in shaping a sustainable future. Apply today and Join our Emergency Management (GHD FIRST) team.

This opportunity can be based out of the Chicago office.

Who is GHD FIRST:

GHD Fast Incident Response Services Team (GHD FIRST) delivers turnkey, 24/7/365 incident response and management services throughout North America. The GHD FIRST team provides the following core services:

Emergency Preparedness, Planning, and Drills
Environmental/ Remediation Services
Incident Management / Incident Command System (ICS)
Air Monitoring/ Industrial Hygiene
Waste Management
Toxicology/ Risk Assessment
Geographic Information Systems (GIS)/ Database
Shoreline Clean-up Assessment Technique (SCAT)
Digital Technology/ Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) Services
Construction/ Construction Management Services
Crisis Communication and Community Engagement
Litigation Support

GHD has more than 100 offices across North America with over 500 staff trained in emergency response and emergency management procedures. Listed below is a management role currently open to grow and further develop the GHD FIRST business sector within GHD.

Working with an energetic and high performing team, this position offers a variety of work and will see you involved in:

Accountable for one or more medium-sized projects of low to moderate complexity with a small- to medium-sized team. Focus on the creation of the project vision and planning documents and manage the implementation, reporting, and performance of the overall project with the expectation of delivering on time, within budget, and to scope.

Document Preparation: Prepare moderately complex documents using a variety of applications for technology devices, such as standard office software. Also responsible for gathering and summarizing data for reports.
Stakeholder Management: Plan and deliver stakeholder engagement activities to develop effective working relationships for projects and to ensure that stakeholder needs and concerns are identified and met.
Personal Capability Building: Develop own capabilities by participating in assessment and development planning activities as well as formal and informal training and coaching; gain or maintain external professional accreditation, where relevant, to improve performance and fulfill personal potential. Maintain an understanding of relevant technology, external regulation, and industry best practices through ongoing education, attending conferences, and reading specialist media.
Continuous Improvement: Contribute to reviewing existing operations in own area of work, and generate new ideas to assist in identifying continuous improvements.
Work Scheduling and Allocation: Assign short-term work schedules to a team of subordinates in order to achieve expectations while following established timelines.
Project Assurance: Conduct assurance reviews within the project, facilitate the delivery of assurance reviews by independent third parties, and take appropriate action to resolve any issues identified, so that senior stakeholders have confidence that the project can deliver according to time, budget, and quality.
Project Scope Definition: Manage the delivery of research, workshops, and other activities to support the specification and agreement of project deliverables.
Project Planning: Produce workstream or project plans, ensuring that all activities are identified, are appropriately organized to deliver project objectives, and comply with the organization's project management framework.
Project Reporting and Review: Draft project review reports and presentations, including key information, commentary, and recommendations, to support the review process and enable stakeholders to evaluate progress and agree on change.
Project Resource Management: Manage the deployment of project resources, proactively managing project costs, providing forecasts, and presenting variances with narrative at appropriate review points to ensure effective utilization.
Project Risk and Issue Management: Identify and evaluate risks, issues, dependencies, and constraints associated with the project, escalating matters where appropriate. Where necessary, develop, agree on, and implement solutions to overcome these concerns.
Project Closeout and Handover: Draft elements of product documentation and user training to support handover to business as usual. Contribute to post-project reviews and identification of lessons learned.
Project Team Management: Lead a small project team; communicate the necessary outcomes and the direction required to achieve them; coordinate team actions on project tasks; request additional team member support when needed; and identify areas of improvement to build the capability of the team through training, coaching, and mentoring.
Requirements Management: Coordinate the identification and elicitation of requirements; conduct analysis of those requirements for completion and alignment; document and manage requirements throughout the life of the project; and coordinate the verification of the end deliverable. Generally done at the level of project phases.
Willingness to respond to call outs during non-routine working hours
Act as the first point of contact for clients for new emergency projects, with ability to delegate tasks and request support as required from GHD FIRST team.

Education

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Engineering, Geology, Environmental Science or a related field

Experience

General Experience: Experience enables job holder to deal with the majority of situations and to advise others (Over 3 years to 6 years)
Managerial Experience: Experience of general supervision of more junior colleagues (7 to 12 months)
Experienced in emergency preparedness, air monitoring, environmental assessment/sampling, ICS, SCAT, PHMSA
Experience with railroad and pipeline related emergencies a plus

Benefits:

401K - Employees are eligible to participate on the first day of the month following 3 months of service
Paid time off – Our PTO benefit is designed to provide eligible employees with a period of rest and relaxation, sick, and personal time throughout the year. PTO starts at 16 days per year and increases with years of service
Holiday Pay - Holiday pay is provided for eligible employees. GHD observes 9 holidays per year. Holiday pay will be based on the regular set schedule for the employee
Wellness Benefit- Regular full-term employees are eligible to participate in the wellness reimbursement program. GHD will reimburse 50% of the cost of the following to maximum of $250.00 reimbursement annually for such items as: Health club membership fees, Home exercise equipment purchases, Bicycles, Race, run & marathon entrance fees, Smoking cessation programs, Weight loss programs (i.e.—Weight Watchers, Jenny Craig), Fitbits and Fitness Tracking devices

Salary: $72,019 - $120,011, varies based on location and experience.

Take on some of the world’s toughest challenges - with everyone at GHD backing you every step of the way.

We'll give you control over your career, empower you to find innovative solutions and help you create a lasting impact.

See where your commitment could take you with GHD.

jobs.description:
**About FACS**


At FACS, our mission is to make environments safer and healthier for the people who live and work in them. As one of the nation's leading environmental health consulting firms, we help organizations protect their people, assets, and communities. We are built on purpose, partnership, and performance, delivering measurable impact with every client engagement.

**Our Values**


We live our mission through three core values:

* **People First:** Support our team and clients, promote professional growth, and value collaboration.
* **Integrity of the Science:** Deliver accurate, reliable results through objective, evidence\-based practices.
* **Client Relationships for Life:** Build long\-term partnerships and help clients address environmental health challenges.

**Why Join Us**

* **Impact:** Contribute meaningful work that empowers teams and drives results across the organization.
* **Culture:** Thrive in a collaborative, entrepreneurial, and mission\-driven environment where your work matters.
* **Growth:** Innovate, develop your skills, and help shape the future of how we operate and deliver on our mission.
* **Visibility:** Partner directly with leadership and cross\-functional teams to make a real difference.


Ranked "Best Places to Work" for five consecutive years, we invest in your success through training, mentorship, and support for professional certifications—so you can grow, thrive, and build a career with lasting impact.

*Curious to see what we do? Meet our team at* FACS Experts.


**About the Role:**


The Environmental Health Specialist will support public health and well\-being by conducting fieldwork and environmental assessments for a variety of environmental health and industrial hygiene projects. Under the direction of Project Managers, you will support projects involving asbestos, lead, mold and moisture, indoor environmental quality, air and exposure sampling, and other environmental health concerns.


This is a field\-based role that requires regular travel to local client sites and occasional travel outside the local area, depending on project needs. You will collect samples and field data, document site conditions, prepare accurate field notes, and communicate project updates to Project Managers.


This opportunity is ideal for someone who enjoys hands\-on work, takes pride in accuracy and professionalism, and is eager to develop technical experience in environmental health and industrial hygiene. The ideal candidate demonstrates strong attention to detail, reliability, a positive work ethic, and a willingness to learn beyond their current comfort zone.

**Responsibilities:**

* Perform assigned fieldwork and project tasks under the direction of Project Managers.
* Travel regularly to local client sites and occasionally to out\-of\-area locations based on project needs.
* Support environmental health and industrial hygiene projects involving asbestos, lead, mold and moisture, indoor environmental quality, air and exposure sampling, and other environmental health concerns.
* Review project scopes, site requirements, and field protocols to ensure a clear understanding of assigned work.
* Collect field data and samples in accordance with established procedures, project specifications, and safety requirements.
* Conduct site observations and document field conditions accurately and thoroughly.
* Prepare, organize, maintain, and transport the tools, equipment, and supplies needed for assigned fieldwork.
* Maintain detailed field notes; compile data; and summarize findings to support project reporting and analysis.
* Communicate regularly with Project Managers regarding project status, technical questions, field conditions, and next steps.
* Report progress, concerns, and deviations from project scope or established protocols promptly.
* Interact professionally and collaboratively with clients, contractors, building occupants, and other stakeholders at project sites.
* Follow all company safety procedures and use required personal protective equipment.
* Participate actively in training, mentorship, and professional\-development opportunities to build technical knowledge in environmental health and industrial hygiene.
* Support the delivery of high\-quality, timely client service while maintaining FACS’s standards for accuracy, professionalism, and integrity.

**What You Bring:**

**Required**

* High school diploma or equivalent.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills and attention to detail.
* Reliable, professional, and able to follow field protocols, safety requirements, and project instructions.
* Valid driver’s license, reliable transportation, current auto insurance, and a driving record that meets company standards.
* Ability to travel regularly to local client sites, with occasional out\-of\-area travel as needed.
* Ability to perform the essential functions of this field\-based role, with or without reasonable accommodation.
* Flexibility to work occasional evenings and weekends based on project requirements.

**Preferred**

* Associate’s or bachelor’s degree in a related field.
* Fieldwork or related experience in environmental services, construction, facilities, EHS, restoration, inspection, sampling, or technical documentation.
* Familiarity with asbestos, lead, mold and moisture, indoor environmental quality, or air and exposure sampling.

**Physical \& Work Requirements**

* Ability to perform field\-based work at client sites, including stooping, kneeling, climbing, crawling, and accessing a variety of areas to collect samples.
* Ability to lift, carry, and move equipment and instruments weighing up to 50 pounds.
* Ability to wear required personal protective equipment and complete job\-related medical surveillance and respirator fit testing, as required for assigned work and consistent with applicable law.
* Ability to work at a desk and use a computer for extended periods to complete documentation and reporting.

jobs.description:
Overview:

Kimley\-Horn's DT Los Angeles, CA office is seeking an Air Quality Professional with 2\-9 years of experience specializing in air quality permitting to join our environmental team. The successful candidates will assist in various projects, assisting industrial and municipal clients with their permitting, compliance, and planning needs.
Responsibilities:
* **Technical Support:**
	+ Assist in conducting air quality impact assessments, analyses, and dispersion modeling.
	+ Perform regulatory and technical analyses in support of permitting project in California and throughout the USA.
	+ Familiar with modeling tools and software including CalEEMod, EMFAC, OFFROAD, CALINE4, AERMOD, CAL3QHCR, ISCST3, AERSCREEN, SCREEN3, and GIS.
* **Report Preparation:**
	+ Prepare technical reports, environmental impact assessments, and documentation.
	+ Conduct air quality impact analyses, health risk assessments, and greenhouse gas analyses.
	+ Assist with the preparation of permit applications and compliance documentation.
* **Field Work:**
	+ Participate in field studies and data collection activities related to air quality.
	+ Participate in compliance audits for environmental topics including air pollutants, toxics, hazardous materials, etc.
* **Data Analysis:**
	+ Perform emission calculations for various industrial processes.
	+ Understanding design documents and engineering drawings.
	+ Utilize Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and other relevant software for environmental analysis.

* Degree (Bachelors or Masters) in Environmental Science, engineering (environmental, chemical, mechanical, civil), atmospheric sciences, physics, chemistry, data science or related field
* 2\-9 years of experience in environmental consulting, with a focus on air quality permitting
* Certified Permitting Professional (CPP) a plus
* Experience with data centers and power production
* Strong understanding of environmental laws, regulations, and standards (e.g., Clean Air Act, CEQA).
* Strong writing/verbal skills

* Positive attitude and a strong work ethic

jobs.title: Senior Environmental Specialist
jobs.description:
Golden State Water Company is one of the largest investor\-owned water utilities in the United States. We deliver quality, reliable water to more than 1 million people in over 80 communities throughout California. Golden State Water has been in business for more than 90 years because we put customers first.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**  

* The Senior Environmental Specialist is a supervisory position that functions as a highly experienced professional specialist responsible for coordinating and directing the Company’s environmental compliance programs. These programs include but are not limited to compliance with National Pollution Discharge Elimination System, California Environmental Quality Act, air quality and hazardous material regulations.
* This position is also responsible for the supervision, development and performance management of the Environmental Specialist.
* This position is responsible for monitoring federal, state and local environmental regulations and legislation, and assisting the General Office, Regions and Districts in compliance with these regulations.
* This position will provide support to the Regions and Districts in preparing technical documents, reports and studies.
* Interprets and recommends actions to comply with applicable federal, state and local laws and regulations. Supports Regions and Districts in compliance activities.
* Oversees any needed Company research activities related to environmental issues. Prepares and implements studies to improve overall environmental quality control. Prepares technical reports and documents to support the Company’s operations including environmental business and functional plans including proposed budgets.
* Analyze proposed legislation, environmental impact reports, environmental documents and environmental regulations that may impact the Company. Consults with internal and external contacts to provide technical expertise and information needed to effectively guide and enable others to comply with applicable policies, rules, regulations and laws.
* Develops and supervises the training and other communications programs for employees to ensure that relevant information and procedures related to environmental health risks are effectively disseminated to management, supervisors, and all other employees. Prepare responses and reports that reflect the best interests of the Company and its customers.
* Initiates, coordinates and participates in environmental audits. Prepares environmental assessments of Company property. Recommend actions to reduce potential environmental hazards.
* Oversees and monitors the maintenance of relevant documentation to ensure accurate and timely record\-keeping for proactive management purposes and to meet regulatory guidelines for documentation and reporting.
* Serve as Company’s representative on environmental committees, both internally and externally.
* Prepare environmental policies, procedures and guidelines to ensure compliance with applicable regulations.
* Performs other duties as assigned.
**MINIMUM POSITION QUALIFICATIONS:**  

* Bachelor’s or Master’s degree from an accredited college or university in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, or other related sciences or related field.
* Five years environmental engineering, regulations and operations experience with demonstrated increasing responsibilities performing highly complex work desired.
* Ten years progressively responsible environmental experience can substitute for a degree.
* Must have excellent verbal and written communication skills.
* Must have and maintain a valid California Driver’s License.


Qualities/Core Competencies:  

* Familiar with database management and able to perform data query
* Good organizational skills
* Attentive to details
* A team player
* Excellent critical and analytical thinking skills.
* Excellent problem solving abilities.

  

May include but not limited to standing, climbing, walking, lifting, bending, pulling and/or pushing, grasping, reaching, stooping and crouching, sitting, typing, walking, reading, writing, color determination, speaking and listening for extended periods of time.**BENEFITS**


Our Company supports our employees with rich benefit programs and resources to help them thrive today and prepare for tomorrow. Benefit options include medical, dental, and vision plans with the Company currently paying 85% of the monthly premium for employees and their eligible dependents. We also offer paid vacation and sick time and twelve Company paid holidays per year. To help our employees plan for the future, we offer both a 401(k) retirement plan as well as a Defined Contribution Profit Sharing retirement plan. Additional benefits include life, AD\&D, and LTD insurance as well as health savings account and flexible spending plans.


**COMPENSATION INFORMATION**


The compensation range provided is in compliance with state specific laws. Multiple factors are used to determine the actual starting rate of pay for all of our positions, including specific skills, years of experience, education, certification(s), and other job related factors.

  

The responsibilities of this position will involve access to information that may be considered confidential, private and sensitive. Therefore, the individual filling this position will be required to both allow and pass a background check.

  

NOTE: Reasonable accommodations will be made to enable individuals with special needs to perform the essential functions.

jobs.title: WATER QUALITY ANALYST
jobs.description:
OPEN COMPETITIVE RECRUITMENT

Open to all qualified candidates

Tentative Examination Dates For This Recruitment

Week of 10/05/26 - Blind Application & Supplemental scoring

Week of 10/19/26 - Oral examination

Under general supervision, to perform a variety of analytical and technical tasks in the administration of the City’s Water Quality Programs; assist the utility in ensuring regulatory compliance with Federal and State water legislation and policy; and perform related work as required.

Essential Functions

Develops, implements and regularly updates the Water Division’s Water Quality and Production programs and trains employees as necessary; participates as a member of the Water Division’s water regulation compliance group; advises the Production/Operations section staff of water quality concerns that may affect treatment and/or operations; assists with oversight of the Water Division’s Cross Connection Control Program; performs analysis and conducts studies; assists in the preparation of water data reports, plans, procedures, specifications, research and the administration of contracts; responds to customer water quality inquiries and complaints; maintains files and databases; compiles data and daily logs of water production, water quality activities and analyzes and interprets results of water tests; participates in consultations with regulatory agencies such as the State Department of Health, Los Angeles County Department of Health Services, Environmental Protection Agency, Regional Water Quality Control Board and other interested parties; assists in the preparation of the applications for the National Pollution Discharge Elimination System(NPDES) permit program and reviews data for compliance of established permits under NPDES; performs periodic review of cross connection program records to ensure compliance to Title 17 requirements; performs laboratory inspections; reviews and updates a variety of basic laboratory procedures for bacteriological testing and qualitative testing of water samples in the laboratory and in the field; reviews laboratory logs and records for accuracy and prepares various reports; develops and implements the water laboratory quality assurance/quality control procedures and maintains documentation; administers contract laboratory services including scheduling, reporting and invoice processing; reviews and interprets laboratory reports; participates in laboratory accreditation and may act as signatory for laboratory reports; attends conferences and meetings related to regulatory compliance of permits and programs implemented by the Water Division; drives on City business.

Minimum Qualifications

Employment Standards:

Knowledge of principles of water treatment and quality tests; regulatory codes and laws relating to the operation of a water system, including but not limited to Title 17 (cross connection) and Title 22 (water quality); NPDES permit program; occupational hazards and safety precautions in the workplace; Federal and State requirements and standards for analyzing potable water; research methods and analytical techniques; modern office procedures, practices and equipment, including but not limited to computer equipment and supporting software.

Skill in Microsoft Office Windows programs, including but not limited to Access, Excel, and Word.

Ability to work according to safety standards; research, analyze, and interpret water quality or environmental regulations or issues and prepare written reports; compile, review, and analyze data; maintain records and files; read and interpret blueprints and diagrams; perform basic laboratory water testing; operate assigned laboratory equipment; communicate effectively both verbally and in writing; establish and maintain effective working relationships with supervisors, fellow employees, the public, and outside agencies.

Education/Training:
Graduation from high school or equivalent, supplemented by two years of technical training, jobexperience and/or college courses such as biology, chemistry, computer applications, environmental science and othersubjects related to water quality and production and three years of recent experience in water quality analysis, or arelated profession in a public or private water utility system or related industry.

License & Certificates:
A valid T-2 Water Treatment Operator certificate issued by the State of California Department of Health Services and a valid D-2 Water Distribution Operator certificate issued by the State of California Department of Health is required within two years of appointment; certification by AWWA or CWEA as a Water Quality Laboratory Analyst Grade I at time of appointment; a valid California Class “C” Driver’s License or equivalent at time of appointment.

Job Description

San Francisco Public Works is seeking a Principal Environmental Specialist at the Project Design and Development division.

Under general direction, the Principal Environmental Specialist manages environmental programs and projects within a defined area of specialty, such as clean air, energy conservation, public outreach, environmental impacts of project construction, NEPA/CEQA compliance, recycling, or toxics and pollution reduction. This position is responsible for planning, coordinating, implementing, and evaluating environmental initiatives and ordinances which include program oversight, staff supervision, budget administration, regulatory interpretation, public communication, and support for policy development and implementation.

Important And Essential Duties

Managing complex environmental programs by developing goals, policies, strategic plans, and standard of protocol/procedures
Supervising and assigning work to program staff
Interpreting and applying relevant environmental laws and regulations
Preparing budgets, monitoring expenditures to ensure adherence to the approved budget, and securing grant funding

Making public presentations, conducting outreach, preparing written communications, and fostering positive partnerships with community groups, nonprofit organizations, commissions and other private and public agencies

jobs.title: Environmental Health Safety Coordinator
jobs.description:
The Environmental, Health, and Safety Coordinator supports EMPWR USA's environmental, health, and safety (EHS) program at the McMinnville food manufacturing facilities. This role provides hands-on support for daily EHS activities, inspections, training, documentation, incident and environmental event response, corrective action follow-up, and employee engagement. The EHS Coordinator works closely with the EHS Manager and partners with Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, Quality, Sanitation, Warehouse, Human Resources, and site leadership to identify and reduce risk, reinforce safe and environmentally responsible work practices, and support a proactive EHS culture.

Responsibilities

EHS Program Support and Coordination

Support the implementation, administration, and continuous improvement of the site EHS management system, policies, procedures, standards, and work practices.
Serve as a visible floor-level EHS resource for employees and leaders, answering questions, reinforcing expectations, and escalating significant concerns to the EHS Manager.
Partner with department leaders and employees to support EHS expectations in daily operations, projects, change management, and continuous improvement activities.
Assist with EHS inspections, observations, communications, action tracking, and other activities that strengthen accountability for safe and environmentally responsible work practices.

Regulatory Compliance

Support compliance with applicable OSHA, Oregon OSHA, EPA, Oregon Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ), and other relevant federal, state, and local EHS requirements.
Maintain required EHS records, logs, documentation, permits, training records, regulatory postings, and other compliance files in an organized and audit-ready manner.
Assist the EHS Manager with regulatory inspections, customer or third-party EHS audits, documentation requests, permit-related activities, and corrective action responses.
Support updates to site programs, training materials, procedures, and records when regulatory or operational requirements change.

Environmental Compliance and Management Support

Support site environmental programs related to waste management, hazardous materials, air emissions, wastewater, stormwater, spill prevention and response, and other applicable environmental requirements.
Assist with routine environmental inspections, monitoring, sampling coordination, recordkeeping, and reporting activities under the direction of the EHS Manager.
Help ensure hazardous, universal, and other regulated wastes are properly identified, labeled, stored, handled, documented, and prepared for disposal in accordance with established procedures.
Maintain environmental records and documentation such as inspection logs, waste records, manifests, vendor documentation, spill records, and permit-related files.
Support environmental incident and spill response activities, including documentation, corrective action tracking, and replenishment of spill response materials.

Occupational Health, Hazard Identification, and Risk Reduction

Conduct routine workplace inspections, safety observations, job hazard analyses, and other proactive hazard identification activities under the direction of the EHS Manager.
Partner with Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, Sanitation, Warehouse, and other functions to identify hazards and support practical risk reduction measures.
Support critical safety and occupational health programs, including lockout/tagout, machine guarding, powered industrial trucks, hazard communication and chemical safety, personal protective equipment, confined space, fall protection, hot work, ergonomics, hearing conservation, respiratory protection, contractor safety, and emergency response, as applicable.
Document identified hazards, track corrective actions to completion, and follow up with responsible owners to help ensure controls remain effective and sustainable.

Incident Investigation and Corrective Action

Respond to workplace injuries, incidents, near misses, environmental releases, spills, and EHS concerns and promptly notify the EHS Manager and appropriate leaders of significant events.
Support investigations by gathering facts, photographs, witness information, documentation, and other relevant evidence, and participate in root-cause analysis as assigned.
Assist with injury, incident, and environmental event documentation, corrective and preventive action tracking, and coordination with Human Resources and operational leaders as appropriate.
Maintain accurate EHS incident files and help identify recurring issues or trends that may require additional corrective action or program improvement.

Training and EHS Culture

Coordinate and deliver new-hire EHS orientation and assigned recurring EHS training for employees, contractors, and visitors.
Maintain accurate training records and assist with scheduling required refresher, department-specific, or compliance training.
Support leaders with safety talks, employee coaching, EHS communications, signage, and timely correction of unsafe conditions, behaviors, or environmental concerns.
Promote employee participation in hazard reporting, near-miss reporting, environmental concern reporting, safety observations, and continuous improvement efforts.
Support the site Safety Committee and other EHS engagement activities by coordinating meetings, preparing materials, documenting minutes, and tracking action items.

Emergency Preparedness and Response

Support emergency action and response programs, drills, inspections, response planning, spill response readiness, and follow-up activities.
Assist with maintaining emergency and spill response equipment, supplies, contact information, and related documentation.
Provide support during workplace emergencies, environmental releases, and other EHS events consistent with training and assigned responsibilities.

EHS Data, Reporting, and Continuous Improvement

Maintain EHS databases, logs, action trackers, inspection records, training records, environmental records, and other systems used to monitor EHS performance and compliance.
Compile EHS metrics, incident information, environmental data, audit findings, training completion data, and corrective action status for review by the EHS Manager and site leadership.
Use observations and available data to identify recurring issues, recommend improvements, and support site EHS initiatives and continuous improvement efforts.

Job Requirements

Associate's or bachelor's degree in environmental health and safety, occupational safety, environmental science, or a related field preferred; equivalent education and relevant experience will be considered.
Minimum of 2 years of environmental, health, and safety experience, preferably in a manufacturing environment; food manufacturing experience is a plus.
Experience conducting workplace inspections, supporting EHS training, maintaining compliance documentation, and participating in incident investigations is preferred.
Working knowledge of OSHA requirements and general manufacturing safety practices; familiarity with environmental compliance requirements and Oregon OSHA or Oregon DEQ experience is preferred.
Familiarity with manufacturing safety programs such as lockout/tagout, machine guarding, powered industrial trucks, chemical safety, PPE, confined space, fall protection, industrial hygiene, and contractor safety.
Experience supporting environmental programs such as hazardous or universal waste, stormwater, wastewater, air emissions, spill prevention and response, or environmental recordkeeping is preferred.
Demonstrated ability to build positive working relationships, communicate EHS expectations effectively, and work collaboratively with employees and leaders at all levels.
Strong written, verbal, facilitation, and training skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and professionally.
Strong organizational and problem-solving skills with attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities and follow corrective actions through completion.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and the ability to learn and use EHS, training, reporting, and compliance management systems.
OSHA 30-Hour training and First Aid/CPR/AED certification are preferred; environmental or hazardous materials training is a plus, and the ability to obtain required training or certifications after hire is expected.
Ability to work in an active manufacturing environment, spend significant time on the production floor, use required PPE, and provide occasional support outside normal business hours when operational, training, or emergency needs require.

jobs.description:
About

Application Filing Deadline: Application filing will be open at least through September 25, 2026 at 11:59PM (PDT), and will close any time thereafter
Location: 505 Paloma Way, Sunol, CA 94586
Recruitment ID: PBT-0922-167137/ RTF0167136-01122585

WHO ARE WE?

San Francisco Public Utilities Commission (SFPUC)

Headquartered in San Francisco, we have 2,300 employees operating across eight counties serving more than 2.7 million customers in the San Francisco Bay Area – 24 hours per day, 365 days per year.

Our Mission
: To provide our customers with high quality, efficient, and reliable water, power, and wastewater services in a manner that values environmental and community interests and sustains the resources entrusted to our care.

Our Vision
: We are an innovative utility leader, recognized for excellent results in service, safety, stewardship, and inclusiveness.

We are an award-winning and industry-leading utilities organization committed to our customers, community interests, and the environment. To learn more about our organization, please visit our website at https://www.sfpuc.org/ .

We are proud of our infrastructure and programs, but most importantly, we value our highly qualified and dedicated workforce which ensures that this vision becomes a reality.

To learn more about working at the SFPUC, visit our career site here .

Role Description

About the Natural Resources and Lands Management Division
: The Natural Resources and Lands Management (NRLM) Division within the Water Enterprise of the SFPUC is responsible for the management of approximately 61,000 acres of Bay Area watershed lands under SFPUC ownership as well as 150 miles of utility right-of-way. The NRLM Division is responsible for managing, protecting, restoring, and monitoring the ecological resources on these lands and environmental compliance for the operations and maintenance of the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System which serves 2.7 million customers. We are committed to responsible natural resources management that protects and restores viable populations of native species and maintains the integrity of the ecosystems that support them for current and future generations. We strive to become a leader in science-based and collaborative environmental stewardship in order to continue providing high-quality and reliable drinking water to our customers.

About The Position

The Programs and Operations Manager provides daily oversight, leadership and strategic direction for the Alameda Creek Watershed Center (ACWC) , advancing its mission as a hub for public education, community engagement, and watershed stewardship. This position oversees daily operations, including the establishment of clear policies and procedures that support safe, consistent, and high quality operations. The Manager supervises staff and volunteers, fostering a high performing and inclusive team environment. The Manager will be a visible, approachable, and supportive leader who builds trust, develops staff, encourages collaboration, and fosters a positive workplace culture where employees and volunteers can thrive. This position is responsible for overseeing the development of high quality educational and interpretive programs, and ensuring a welcoming and meaningful experience for all visitors. The Manager plays a leadership role in shaping the Center’s public identity, developing partnerships, and leading community engagement efforts that support SFPUC’s mission of service, stewardship, and equity. This position works collaboratively across the Division and the SFPUC on planning and programming efforts that strengthen public understanding of the Alameda Creek Watershed, local ecology, cultural history, and the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System. The role requires initiative, sound judgment, and a commitment to equity, public service, and environmental stewardship.

Work Schedule:
Tuesday through Saturday with occasional work on evenings and Sundays for special events, subject to change if necessary.

Working Relationship:
This position will report to the Alameda Watershed Resources Manager and will supervise a team of staff and volunteers. Initially this position will supervise the ACWC Facility Coordinator and the Education and Volunteers Coordinator, along with 6 part-time staff and several volunteers. This position will require professional, welcoming and friendly interactions with the public and community/agency partners. This position will require collaboration with the facilities team, communications, staff and managers throughout the division, key staff in PUC, including the Assistant General Manager for the Water Enterprise.

Nature of Work:
Portion of the work duties will be outdoors, exposing the incumbent to inclement weather, potential hazards, and animals common in a natural landscape. The position may stand and/or walk for extended periods of time. Ability to work in a busy, noisy environment. Occasionally may lift and/or push 30 pounds of equipment.

Essential duties and responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Strategic Operations and Facility Management

Provide daily oversight of facility operations to ensure a safe, welcoming, and mission aligned visitor experience.
Lead the development and implementation of operational policies and procedures that guide facility use, visitor services, safety practices, and daily operations.
Oversee the aquarium, exhibits, grounds, and community spaces to ensure safe, high quality and consistent standards.
Direct the care, protection, and organization of collections and interpretive materials.
Oversee safety, security, and emergency preparedness efforts in alignment with SFPUC policies and regulatory requirements.
Coordinate maintenance and repairs with the facilities team and contractors, proactively identifying operational needs and improvements.

Interpretation, Education, and Program Leadership

Provide leadership for the development and delivery of interpretive, educational, and public programs that support SFPUC goals and community needs.
Establish interpretive themes related to watershed ecology, cultural and tribal history, and the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System.
Develop program guidelines, procedures, and quality standards to ensure consistency and excellence across offerings.
Evaluate program effectiveness and develop summary reports using data and community feedback, supporting continuous improvement.
Maintain subject matter expertise in regional natural and cultural history and SFPUC systems.

Community Engagement and Partnership Development

Lead outreach, community engagement, and communications strategies that increase visibility and participation in ACWC programs.
Build and sustain partnerships with public agencies, schools, community based organizations, tribal representatives and local governments.
Represent the ACWC, the Division, and the SFPUC at public meetings, professional conferences, and community events.
Support initiatives that strengthen community relationships, advance equity, and expand access to programs and services.

Staff and Volunteer Leadership

Build and maintain staff capacity to ensure the ACWC is fully and reliably staffed for public operating hours, programs, and special events
Develop staff guidelines, volunteer protocols, and workflow procedures to support consistent operations.
Lead staff development, performance management, scheduling, and training.
Oversee volunteer recruitment, onboarding, training, and engagement programs.
Provide coaching, and support to staff and volunteers, promoting a collaborative, inclusive, and service oriented culture.

Administration and Strategic Planning

Manage budgets, contracts, procurement, and HR related processes in alignment with SFPUC policies.
Develop and maintain administrative policies and procedures that support efficient, compliant, and transparent operations.
Contribute to strategic planning and the development of long term goals, policies, and operational plans for the Division and SFPUC.
Prepare reports and performance metrics that support accountability and continuous improvement.

Ideal Candidate And Competencies

The ideal candidate will have a demonstrated track record and ability to exercise the following leadership competencies which are critical for success in the role of Alameda Creek Watershed Center Programs and Operations Manager at SFPUC's Natural Resources & Lands Management Division.

Relationship Management: Builds open, honest, and respectful relationships through effective communication and collaboration techniques. Develops networks and lasting partnerships across boundaries to maintain strategic relationships and achieve common goals. Utilizes a variety of communication approaches to successfully gain support, influence others, and strengthen relationship.

How To Qualify

Minimum Qualifications:
Minimum qualifications reflect the lowest level of acceptable education and/or experience required of an individual such that the individual reasonably could be expected to satisfactorily perform the duties of the position. Candidates must meet all the requirements established by the MQs to be considered for the position.

Education: Possession of a baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university
Experience: Five (5) years of professional work experience coordinating or directing environmental stewardship, education or related community programs in visitor services, educational programming, interpretive center operations, or community engagement; Experience managing budgets, contracts, or administrative processes and collaborating with community partners, public agencies, educators, or local governments.
License: Possession of a valid and current California driver’s license.

Substitution:
Additional qualifying professional experience may substitute for the education requirement on a year for year basis for up to 2 years. One (1) year is equivalent to thirty (30) semester units/forty-five (45) quarter units.

Note: One year of full-time employment is equivalent to 2000 hours. (2000 hours of qualifying work experience is based on a 40-hour work week.)

Applicants must meet the minimum qualification requirement by the final filing date unless otherwise noted. Applicants who meet the minimum qualifications are not guaranteed to advance through all of the steps in the selection process.

Desirable Qualifications

The stated desirable qualifications may be used to identify job finalists at the end of the selection process when candidates are referred for hiring.

Supervisory experience with staff and volunteers interacting with the public.
Experience developing or implementing policies, procedures, or standard operating guidelines for community, non-profit or public facilities, such as visitor centers or education centers.
Experience supporting operations for a community facility (opening/closing, safety procedures, coordinating maintenance and repairs).

WHO ARE WE?

San Francisco Public Utilities Commission (SFPUC)

Headquartered in San Francisco, we have 2,300 employees operating across eight counties serving more than 2.7 million customers in the San Francisco Bay Area – 24 hours per day, 365 days per year.

Our Mission
: To provide our customers with high quality, efficient, and reliable water, power, and wastewater services in a manner that values environmental and community interests and sustains the resources entrusted to our care.

Our Vision
: We are an innovative utility leader, recognized for excellent results in service, safety, stewardship, and inclusiveness.

We are an award-winning and industry-leading utilities organization committed to our customers, community interests, and the environment. To learn more about our organization, please visit our website at https://www.sfpuc.org/.

We are proud of our infrastructure and programs, but most importantly, we value our highly qualified and dedicated workforce which ensures that this vision becomes a reality.

To learn more about working at the SFPUC, visit our career site here.

Role description

About the Natural Resources and Lands Management Division
: The Natural Resources and Lands Management (NRLM) Division within the Water Enterprise of the SFPUC is responsible for the management of approximately 61,000 acres of Bay Area watershed lands under SFPUC ownership as well as 150 miles of utility right-of-way. The NRLM Division is responsible for managing, protecting, restoring, and monitoring the ecological resources on these lands and environmental compliance for the operations and maintenance of the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System which serves 2.7 million customers. We are committed to responsible natural resources management that protects and restores viable populations of native species and maintains the integrity of the ecosystems that support them for current and future generations. We strive to become a leader in science-based and collaborative environmental stewardship in order to continue providing high-quality and reliable drinking water to our customers.

About The Position

The Programs and Operations Manager provides daily oversight, leadership and strategic direction for the Alameda Creek Watershed Center (ACWC), advancing its mission as a hub for public education, community engagement, and watershed stewardship. This position oversees daily operations, including the establishment of clear policies and procedures that support safe, consistent, and high quality operations. The Manager supervises staff and volunteers, fostering a high performing and inclusive team environment. The Manager will be a visible, approachable, and supportive leader who builds trust, develops staff, encourages collaboration, and fosters a positive workplace culture where employees and volunteers can thrive. This position is responsible for overseeing the development of high quality educational and interpretive programs, and ensuring a welcoming and meaningful experience for all visitors. The Manager plays a leadership role in shaping the Center’s public identity, developing partnerships, and leading community engagement efforts that support SFPUC’s mission of service, stewardship, and equity. This position works collaboratively across the Division and the SFPUC on planning and programming efforts that strengthen public understanding of the Alameda Creek Watershed, local ecology, cultural history, and the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System. The role requires initiative, sound judgment, and a commitment to equity, public service, and environmental stewardship.

Work Schedule:
Tuesday through Saturday with occasional work on evenings and Sundays for special events, subject to change if necessary.

Working Relationship:
This position will report to the Alameda Watershed Resources Manager and will supervise a team of staff and volunteers. Initially this position will supervise the ACWC Facility Coordinator and the Education and Volunteers Coordinator, along with 6 part-time staff and several volunteers. This position will require professional, welcoming and friendly interactions with the public and community/agency partners. This position will require collaboration with the facilities team, communications, staff and managers throughout the division, key staff in PUC, including the Assistant General Manager for the Water Enterprise.

Nature of Work:
Portion of the work duties will be outdoors, exposing the incumbent to inclement weather, potential hazards, and animals common in a natural landscape. The position may stand and/or walk for extended periods of time. Ability to work in a busy, noisy environment. Occasionally may lift and/or push 30 pounds of equipment.

Essential duties and responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Strategic Operations and Facility Management

Provide daily oversight of facility operations to ensure a safe, welcoming, and mission aligned visitor experience.
Lead the development and implementation of operational policies and procedures that guide facility use, visitor services, safety practices, and daily operations.
Oversee the aquarium, exhibits, grounds, and community spaces to ensure safe, high quality and consistent standards.
Direct the care, protection, and organization of collections and interpretive materials.
Oversee safety, security, and emergency preparedness efforts in alignment with SFPUC policies and regulatory requirements.
Coordinate maintenance and repairs with the facilities team and contractors, proactively identifying operational needs and improvements.

Interpretation, Education, and Program Leadership

Provide leadership for the development and delivery of interpretive, educational, and public programs that support SFPUC goals and community needs.
Establish interpretive themes related to watershed ecology, cultural and tribal history, and the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System.
Develop program guidelines, procedures, and quality standards to ensure consistency and excellence across offerings.
Evaluate program effectiveness and develop summary reports using data and community feedback, supporting continuous improvement.
Maintain subject matter expertise in regional natural and cultural history and SFPUC systems.

Community Engagement and Partnership Development

Lead outreach, community engagement, and communications strategies that increase visibility and participation in ACWC programs.
Build and sustain partnerships with public agencies, schools, community based organizations, tribal representatives and local governments.
Represent the ACWC, the Division, and the SFPUC at public meetings, professional conferences, and community events.
Support initiatives that strengthen community relationships, advance equity, and expand access to programs and services.

Staff and Volunteer Leadership

Build and maintain staff capacity to ensure the ACWC is fully and reliably staffed for public operating hours, programs, and special events
Develop staff guidelines, volunteer protocols, and workflow procedures to support consistent operations.
Lead staff development, performance management, scheduling, and training.
Oversee volunteer recruitment, onboarding, training, and engagement programs.
Provide coaching, and support to staff and volunteers, promoting a collaborative, inclusive, and service oriented culture.

Administration and Strategic Planning

Manage budgets, contracts, procurement, and HR related processes in alignment with SFPUC policies.
Develop and maintain administrative policies and procedures that support efficient, compliant, and transparent operations.
Contribute to strategic planning and the development of long term goals, policies, and operational plans for the Division and SFPUC.
Prepare reports and performance metrics that support accountability and continuous improvement.

Ideal Candidate And Competencies

The ideal candidate will have a demonstrated track record and ability to exercise the following leadership competencies which are critical for success in the role of Alameda Creek Watershed Center Programs and Operations Manager at SFPUC's Natural Resources & Lands Management Division.

Relationship Management: Builds open, honest, and respectful relationships through effective communication and collaboration techniques. Develops networks and lasting partnerships across boundaries to maintain strategic relationships and achieve common goals. Utilizes a variety of communication approaches to successfully gain support, influence others, and strengthen relationship.

How to qualify

Minimum Qualifications:
Minimum qualifications reflect the lowest level of acceptable education and/or experience required of an individual such that the individual reasonably could be expected to satisfactorily perform the duties of the position. Candidates must meet all the requirements established by the MQs to be considered for the position.

Education: Possession of a baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university
Experience: Five (5) years of professional work experience coordinating or directing environmental stewardship, education or related community programs in visitor services, educational programming, interpretive center operations, or community engagement; Experience managing budgets, contracts, or administrative processes and collaborating with community partners, public agencies, educators, or local governments.
License: Possession of a valid and current California driver’s license.

Substitution:
Additional qualifying professional experience may substitute for the education requirement on a year for year basis for up to 2 years. One (1) year is equivalent to thirty (30) semester units/forty-five (45) quarter units.

Note: One year of full-time employment is equivalent to 2000 hours. (2000 hours of qualifying work experience is based on a 40-hour work week.)

Applicants must meet the minimum qualification requirement by the final filing date unless otherwise noted. Applicants who meet the minimum qualifications are not guaranteed to advance through all of the steps in the selection process.

Desirable Qualifications

The stated desirable qualifications may be used to identify job finalists at the end of the selection process when candidates are referred for hiring.

Supervisory experience with staff and volunteers interacting with the public.

Company Description

Veolia in North America is the top-ranked environmental company in the United States for three consecutive years, and the country’s largest private water operator and technology provider as well as hazardous waste and pollution treatment leader. It offers a full spectrum of water, waste, and energy management services, including water and wastewater treatment, commercial and hazardous waste collection and disposal, energy consulting and resource recovery. Veolia helps commercial, industrial, healthcare, higher education and municipality customers throughout North America. Headquartered in Boston, Veolia has more than 10,000 employees working at more than 350 locations across North America.

Job Description

Position Purpose:

This position provides specialized transportation and disposal services to our clients. Responsibilities include manifesting, packaging, spill response, labeling, loading/unloading, coordinating transportation, and sampling/profiling material while adhering to state and federal environmental, health, and safety regulations.

Primary Duties /Responsibilities

Sample waste streams according to prescribed policies and procedures.
Manifesting, packaging, spill clean-up response and remedial activities, labeling, loading, off loading, and coordinating transportation.
Maintain a professional image to clients by answering inquiries and suggesting solutions to existing/potential problems.
Comply and enforce all compliance, health, safety, and procedures in accordance with VES-TS policies.
Become familiar with all U. S. Department of Transportation (DOT)/Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and VES-TS regulations required in submitting paperwork to expedite disposal of hazardous waste.
Operate and maintain all equipment in a professional manner to ensure optimum efficiency and effectiveness.
Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Education / Experience / Background:

High School diploma or General Educational Development (GED) required
Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry or a related science discipline preferred

Knowledge / Skills / Abilities

Strong team player
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills
Time management: the ability to organize and manage multiple deadlines
Strong customer service orientation
Computer proficiency
Ability to follow through on assignments.

Required Certification / Licenses / Training

40-hour HAZWOPER Certification
Valid Driver's License
Ability to obtain a Class A or B Commercial Drivers License (CDL) with Hazardous (H) endorsement

Veolia’s comprehensive benefits package includes paid time off policies, as well as health, dental, vision, life insurance, savings accounts, tuition reimbursement, paid volunteering and more. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer! All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status.

### **Job Description and Duties**


Are you looking to be a part of a dynamic team of conservation\-minded scientists working to protect fish and wildlife resources in the coniferous forests of the Sierra Nevada (covering counties: Plumas, Butte, Sierra, Yuba, Nevada, Placer, El Dorado, Alpine, Amador and Calaveras), or the Coastal Mountain Range in Lake County?


The Department of Fish and Wildlife's Timberland Conservation and Fire Resiliency Program is seeking a motivated professional to work as an Environmental Scientist reviewing and evaluating Timber Harvest Plans,Timber Emergencies and Exemptions, and Vegetation Management Plans. This position also works in close collaboration with other Environmental Scientists and Senior Environmental Scientists, and with other state agencies as part of an interdisciplinary review team and may act as the staff lead and may provide consultative advice when working with applicants, local, state and federal agencies, stakeholders, and the general public.


Under the close supervision of a Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory), and as a member of the California Department of Fish and Wildlife’s (Department) North Central Region (Region 2\) Timberland Conservation and Fire Resiliency Program, the incumbent is responsible for conducting identified activities related to the Forest Practice Rules, the Department’s Lake and Streambed Alteration Program (LSA), the California Endangered Species Act (CESA), the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), and other laws, regulations, and Department policies, guidelines, and procedures pertaining to the protection of biological resources. The incumbent represents the Region and may act as the staff lead and provide consultative advice when working with applicants, local, state, and federal agencies, stakeholders, and the general public. Public contacts made in the course of this work are sensitive and involve a wide variety of special interest groups.


**Personal Leave Program:** Effective July 1, 2025, state employees are subject to temporary salary reductions ranging from 2% to 4\.62% in exchange for Personal Leave Program (PLP) hours. Please note that the salary ranges listed in this Job Control may not reflect these reductions associated with the 2025 Personal Leave Program.


Please follow the link for more information regarding the 2025 Personal Leave program: Personal Leave Program \- Human Resources \- CalHR.


This position may be eligible for a telework opportunity in accordance with departmental policies and operational needs. Beginning July 1, 2026, employees will be required to work in\-person at least four (4\) days per week in alignment with Executive Order N\-22\-25\. Additional in\-office days may be required based on operational needs.


Link to Environmental Scientist Exam: CalCareers


**This position is a 12\-month Limited Term (LT) and may be extended up to 24 months or become permanent.** During this 12\-month Limited Term assignment, you will receive full health, dental, and vision benefits! You will also earn State Service and accrue monthly leave credits.


You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


This position is eligible for partial telework (1\-day per week) based upon program need and will be headquartered from the Rancho Cordova regional office located at 1701 Nimbus Road, Rancho Cordova, CA 95670\. Based on institutional need, this position may be located in alternate locations and will be provided flexible hoteling space at any of the North Central Region's offices. This position requires the use of a computer for several hours each day, the completion of office tasks that require sitting, standing, and walking to other locations; attendance at meetings and participation in conference calls. The position may require occasional travel throughout the State for site visits (30% of work time) including overnight travel, early mornings, and late nights. Must be able to work unusual and/or long hours; travel frequently; spend multiple days in the field assessing habitat conditions in inclement weather; walk in and through rough terrain; hike over uneven, steep, wet, and rough terrain with no vehicle access; operate a four\-wheel drive (4WD) vehicle off highway and over rough terrain; operate an all\-terrain vehicle (ATV); operate office equipment (computers, copies/scanners, telephones, iPads, global positioning system \[GPS] units, etc.); must possess a valid driver's license and be prepared to travel using a state vehicle with short notice for extended periods. The position requires the use of personal protective equipment, including, but not limited to, protective footwear, hardhat, gloves, helmet, and eye protection. Wearing a Department of Fish and Wildlife uniform is required as a condition of employment while conducting field work and public work duties on occasion.
