Job Description And Duties

The Measurement Assessment and Research Section (MARS) operates one of the Mobile Source Emissions Testing Facilities within the Mobile Source Laboratory Division (MSLD), equipped with Portable Emissions Measurement Systems (PEMS) and Portable Emissions Acquisition Systems (PEAQS) to generate high-quality, legally defensible emissions data. MARS’s mission is to support the development and implementation of heavy-duty on-road and off-road vehicle regulations, strengthen emissions inventories, inform enforcement actions, advance the Clean Truck Check program, and support innovative emissions research. Through surveillance testing of in-use on-road and off-road heavy-duty vehicles and equipment, MARS provides critical insights into real-world emissions performance and regulatory effectiveness. MARS also serves as a platform for evaluating and demonstrating new testing approaches, developing innovative methods for measuring in-use emissions, and expanding CARB’s testing capabilities. In collaboration with CARB mobile source workgroups, MARS develops and executes comprehensive test plans, conducts emissions testing, and performs robust data analyses to inform policy and regulatory decisions. Collectively, these efforts provide a scientific foundation for reducing criteria pollutants, greenhouse gases, and toxic air contaminants from the heavy-duty sector and protecting public health and air quality.

MARS is seeking an Air Pollution Specialist to perform complex technical work related to in-use emissions characterization of heavy-duty (HD) on-road and off-road vehicles and equipment. The incumbent will perform on-road emissions measurements with portable emissions measurement systems (PEMS) and the Portable Emissions Acquisition System (PEAQS), and ensure compliance with established test procedures, data quality objectives, and safety protocols. Duties include developing and applying analytical methods for emissions data processing, validation, and interpretation; analyzing large datasets using computational tools; designing and executing test plans; operating advanced emissions measurement systems; coordinating test resources; and preparing technical reports in support of regulatory programs, research initiatives, and emissions assessments, while working independently and collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team to support CARB’s mission to protect air quality.

This position offers a balanced mix of laboratory, field, and office-based work and supports CARB’s mission by advancing in-use emissions measurement techniques and evaluating emerging heavy-duty vehicle technologies. The incumbent's position may require Statewide travel up to 30% of the time for fieldwork, training or for meetings.

jobs.description:
**PROJECT:** Moffett Federal Airfield at Moffett Field, CA 94035 with Avports LLC

**DEPARTMENT:**Airfield Management

**TITLE:** Safety, Environmental and Health (SEH) Manager

**PAY RANGE:** $100,000 \- $115,00 Annually

**REPORTS TO:** Airfield Manager

**Responsibility Level:**


Responsible for the development, implementation, and monitoring of Avports Safety, Environmental and Health (SEH) Programs, including the IS\-BAH (International Standard for Business Aircraft Handling) and Safety Management System (SMS) at Moffett Federal Airfield. The chief goal is to establish a safety culture that strives to protect employees/customers, the environment and business operations.


This is a full\-time benefited salaried position.

**Essential Duties:**

* Manage all Safety, Environmental and Health Programs at Moffett Federal Airfield, provides regular reports to management on program status and compliance.
* Develop, implement and monitor an employee SEH training program to ensure compliance with Company requirements, applicable Cal/OSHA, OSHA, CalEPA, NATA (National Air Transportation Association), and IS\-BAH and SMS standards.
* Manage, regularly update and review training programs, maintain accurate employee training records to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements.
* Develop training materials and provides employee training as necessary for such programs as Injury Illness Prevention Plan (IIPP), Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure (SPCC), Stormwater Pollution Prevention (SWPP), Hazard Communication, Building Emergency Action Plan, Hearing Protection Program, Lock Out Tag Out, Fall Protection, and other EHS programs.
* Ensures that all staff complete any mandated EHS training assigned by the company or regulatory agencies, and maintain training completion records.
* Monitors compliance with applicable regulatory EHS standards and develop, updates all program manuals, plans, SOPs, training materials as required.
* Serves as Chair of the Safety Committee and holds monthly safety committee meetings with designated staff. Responsible for keeping meeting records to track and report progress. Also serves on the Company wide Safety Committee that meets quarterly.
* Track all safety performance indicators and generate administrative reports to monitor trends, identify areas of concern, and support continuous improvement.
* Write and review job hazard analysis, job safety analysis and implement safe work practices.
* Investigates all incidents, accidents, near miss events and hazardous conditions. Conducts risk management, root cause analysis and ensures implementation of corrective actions to mitigate risks.
* Conducts regular workplace safety, SPCC and internal IS\-BAH audits to verify compliance.
* Coordinate and serve as safety liaison for regulatory inspections, external IS\-BAH and customer audits and environmental assessments.
* Secures and maintains environmental compliance permits with pertinent regulatory agencies.
* Holds regular safety briefings with employees to promote EHS programs.
* Assures compliance with standards and regulations relating to ground transportation, FBO, ramp procedures, and best management practices.
* Purchases inventory, distribution and maintain uniforms and safety equipment in a safe, clean, neat and orderly manner. Ensure all staff are provided and trained on the use of PPE.
* Maintains Ramp Safety Program and enforces airport rules and regulations through the Airfield Access and Driver’s Training program.
* Oversee the Hazardous Waste Storage area and ensure regulatory agency compliance through regular inspections (i.e. labelling, containment, proper disposal, documentation, etc.).
* Creates and manages a Environmental, Health and Safety Employee Incentive Program.
* Acts as safety liaison for airfield projects with outside contractors/vendors/organizations to oversee EHS compliance.
* Provides assistance and recommendations on EHS issues to management.
* Upholds all Company and EHS procedures and policies.
* Performs other duties as assigned.

**Required Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:**

  

* Excellent communication, organizational and technical writing skills required.
* Strong Computer skills required.
* Knowledge and experience with implementing Cal/OSHA, OSHA, Cal/EPA, EPA, BAAQM regulations and training.
* Knowledge and experience in the aviation operations industry.
* Experience in developing and managing various EHS programs in an aviation work environment.

 **Licenses, Registrations and/or Certificates:**

  

* Must pass mandatory drug screenings, criminal background checks \& obtain security clearance.
* Must maintain a valid Class C motor vehicle operator’s license as issued by the State of California.
* Completion of a Professional Line Service Technician Certification within six months of hire date.
* Completion of the IS\-BAH program workshop within six months of hire date.
* Completion of Safety Management System for Managers within six months of hire date.
* Completion of ALL Cal/OSHA required training within the first 90 days of hire date.
* Completion of ALL other Certificates/Licenses as deemed necessary within one year of hire date.

 **Education:**

  

* Bachelor Degree in Safety Engineering, Occupational Safety and Health or related field preferred.
* Certified Safety Professional credential preferred.

 **Experience:**

  

* Five years of Occupational Safety experience in the aviation industry or similar setting.Equivalent combination of acceptable training and experience may be considered by the HR Manager and Airport Manager.

Discover your full potential. At Tetra Tech, we are collaborating with industry-leading experts for a sustainable future for our world. We combine consulting and engineering with advanced analytics and technology to solve the world’s most complex challenges. Our innovation hubs across the globe will enable you to share ideas and best practices while growing your professional network. Wherever you are in your career journey, you will benefit from working with world-class engineers, scientists, and technical specialists.

At Tetra Tech, we are Leading with Science to solve the world’s most complex challenges. Our industry-leading experts in engineering and consulting are committed to driving positive change in communities around the world. For over 50 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. Today we stand as a market leader, offering cutting-edge solutions in water, environment, energy, and international development. Our work has improved more than 625 million lives around the world.

Join Tetra Tech to make a real difference. Our work leverages cutting-edge technologies, advanced analytics, and the expertise of world-class scientists and engineers to create meaningful change around the world. Discover your full potential – join us to advance your career while leaving a lasting legacy.

Apply today and join the company that is Leading with Science®.

Tetra Tech is seeking a self-motivated, Entry-Level Environmental Scientist / Compliance Specialist to support and expand our landfill and air quality compliance services within the solid waste industry. This position is ideal for candidates with a strong interest in air regulations, landfill gas systems, emissions compliance, and environmental data analysis.

In this role, you will support regulatory compliance programs by analyzing field and operational data, interpreting air quality regulations and permit requirements, preparing compliance reports, and assisting with air permitting and emissions calculations. The primary focus areas include landfill gas monitoring, Surface Emissions Monitoring (SEM), Landfill Gas-to-Energy (LFGTE) Systems, air quality permitting, and compliance with New Source Performance Standards (NSPS) and National Emissions Standards for Hazardous Pollutants (NESHAP) regulations applicable to solid waste facilities.

This position is primarily remote, with limited, as-needed travel or occasional site visits. Only those in PST or MST will be considered.
Candidates must be comfortable working independently with limited supervision while collaborating with project managers, field staff, engineers, and regulatory specialists across geographically dispersed teams.

This position is eligible for our full benefits package including but not limited to Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, AD&D, Disability, Flexible Spending Account (FSA), Health Spending Account (HSA), My Flex Time (MFT - paid time off), 401K, and an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. The pay range for this position is $55K-$75K annually, based on qualifications, location, and experience. Only those that attach a cover letter will be considered.
The deadline to apply is 09/3/2026.

Your Role

Review, analyze, and interpret landfill air quality and landfill gas monitoring data, including wellfield data, SEM, and air emissions datasets.
Compare monitoring and operational data against regulatory standards, permit limits, and NSPS/NESHAP criteria to assess compliance.
Prepare environmental compliance reports, including air compliance summaries, monitoring reports, deviation analyses, and regulatory submittals.
Support the development and preparation of air quality permit applications, amendments, and renewals, including emission calculations and regulatory compliance demonstrations.
Collect, manage, track, and organize large datasets related to air emissions, landfill gas, SEM results, and compliance deadlines.
Develop and maintain templates, trackers, and tools to support consistent, accurate, and timely reporting for multiple facilities / landfills.
Coordinate with on-site operations, technicians, and subcontractors to confirm that monitoring, testing, and system performance meet regulatory and permit requirements.
Support Project Managers with deliverables, schedules, and client coordination including procurement of supplies, subcontractor coordination and Work Order development.
Contribute to multidisciplinary teams on engineering, permitting, and environmental projects.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, or a related field.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, including technical and regulatory writing.
Proficiency in MS Office – specifically Word and Excel.
Ability to work independently in a remote environment, demonstrate initiative, and manage multiple priorities with limited supervision.
Strong interpersonal skills and ability to collaborate effectively with field staff, engineers, and regulatory agencies.
Valid driver’s license.
Ability and willingness to perform limited travel as required.
Interest and ability in developing technical and leadership skills within the Environmental Compliance field.

Life At Tetra Tech

The perks of working at Tetra Tech include:

Comprehensive and market-competitive benefits.
Merit-based financial rewards.
Flexibility and company-wide commitment to work/life balance.
Collaborative team atmosphere that values the contributions of all employees.
Learning and development opportunities for ongoing professional growth.

With 25,000 employees working together, Tetra Tech provides clear solutions to complex problems by Leading with Science® to address the entire water cycle, protect and restore the environment, design sustainable and resilient infrastructure, and support the clean energy transition.

### **Job Description and Duties**


The Department Fish and Wildlife's Northern Region Inland Fisheries and Wild Trout unit has an opening for a Limited Term Environmental Scientist. The incumbent will be part of a team of scientists working to survey high elevation aquatic habitats across California's northern nine counties and conduct restoration activities within the Trinity Alps Wilderness, Russian Wilderness and Marble Mountain Wilderness areas. This project seeks to reduce the compounding effects from drought, climate change, and invasive predators on declining native amphibians by identifying and actively managing invasive fish populations in key drought\-resilient lake basins and restoring sensitive amphibians to suitable habitats within their historic range.
  

  

We are seeking a highly motivated individual to join our team in a position that provides development of expertise in fisheries and herpetology science and management, survey and study design, designing, implementing, and monitoring habitat restoration projects, data analysis utilizing statistical methods, and scientific writing. This position will require a significant commitment to backcountry work, hiking, camping, and operating 4\-wheel drive vehicles in remote high mountain environments. Overnight travel, including backpacking and car camping, will be required.  

  

  



**Personal Leave Program:** Effective July 1, 2025, state employees are subject to temporary salary reductions ranging from 2% to 4\.62% in exchange for Personal Leave Program (PLP) hours. Please note that the salary ranges listed in this Job Control may not reflect these reductions associated with the 2025 Personal Leave Program.  

Please follow the link for more information regarding the 2025 Personal Leave program:  

Personal Leave Program \- Human Resources \- CalHR.  

  

In order to be eligible for this position, you must either be transfer eligible or take and pass the following exam.  

Class Title: Environmental Scientist  

  

**This position is a 12\-month Limited Term (LT) and may be extended up to 24 months or become permanent.**  

  

During this 12\-month Limited Term assignment, you will receive full health, dental, and vision benefits! You will also earn State Service and accrue monthly leave credits.
You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


This position requires indoor work at an office location and outdoor work in remote environments.
  

  

The indoor work (approximately 60%) requires the ability to use a computer and a suite of various software necessary for data storage/retrieval, analysis, and report writing. Will plan field work, coordinate with seasonal staff, attend meetings, maintain and organize project gear/equipment, and work with staff and interested parties statewide to complete work assignments.
  

  

The outdoor work (approximately 40%) requires time in a high elevation backcountry wilderness setting, in rugged terrain with hot and freezing conditions and hazardous organisms; overnight travel, including up to eight days of backpacking or car camping is required. The ability to drive a 4\-wheel\-drive vehicle and use of a state\-owned vehicle for travel is required between remote facilities and field sites where public transportation is not readily available. Must wear a uniform when engaging with the public and conducting field work.

### **Job Description and Duties**


Under the direction of the Nutria Eradication Operations Supervisor, the incumbent will support the Department's Nutria Eradication Program. Nutria are highly invasive and extremely detrimental to the environment, but primarily nocturnal and relatively elusive in low densities. This position is physically demanding, but highly rewarding given the ultimate accomplishment of protecting California's wetlands, waterways, infrastructure, and agriculture. As part of a team, the incumbent will contribute to surveys to detect, locate, and trap nutria, with the ultimate goal of eradicating nutria from the state. Duties include: Under the supervision of the Nutria Eradication Operations Supervisor, the incumbent will serve as one of the lead field scientists for the Nutria Eradication Program. Nutria are highly invasive and extremely detrimental to the environment, but primarily nocturnal and relatively elusive in low densities. This position will play a critical role in the coordination of field crews conducting nutria surveys and trapping across the northern portion of the nutria infestation. The incumbent will assist the Operations Supervisor with training, leading, and evaluating field crew technicians and scientific aides to survey for, detect, and remove nutria, with the ultimate goal of eradicating nutria from the State of California. The incumbent will lead the team by example in conducting habitat suitability assessments, visual observation and camera surveys, trapping, and electronic data collection (i.e., ESRI Collector smartphone application), as well as effective use of baits and lures and obtaining entry permits from local landowners. The incumbent is responsible for conducting morning briefings of the assigned crew, tracking daily spatial assignments, and ensuring field staff understand understand project protocols. The incumbent will work with the Operations Supervisors, other field crew leads, and Planning Specialist to evaluate and help refine detection and trapping methods and tools for the most effective and efficient detection and removal of nutria. The incumbent will also closely coordinate with other regions and Department functions, as well as other affected and involved local, State, and Federal agencies. Work includes preparing draft reports and correspondence and answering routine questions from the public relative to Departmental nutria efforts. The primary geographical focus of this position will be in San Joaquin, Sacramento, Contra Costa, Solano, Alameda, and Calaveras counties, but work may be assigned in any part of the area of nutria infestation. This position is physically demanding, but highly rewarding given the ultimate accomplishment of protecting California's wetlands, waterways, infrastructure, and agriculture from the devastation nutria have caused in other regions of North America. Incumbent must be willing and able to competently use firearms as per the Department’s Policy for Non\-Enforcement Personnel.  

  

  



**Personal Leave Program:** Effective July 1, 2025, state employees are subject to temporary salary reductions ranging from 2% to 4\.62% in exchange for Personal Leave Program (PLP) hours. Please note that the salary ranges listed in this Job Control may not reflect these reductions associated with the 2025 Personal Leave Program.  

Please follow the link for more information regarding the 2025 Personal Leave program:  

Personal Leave Program \- Human Resources \- CalHR.

### **Working Conditions**


Be willing to work atypical hours and on weekends. Some overnight travel (\<5%) may be required. Able to swim, walk through deep mud and thick vegetation, work on steep or uneven terrain, in extreme weather and under physically challenging conditions. Be willing and able to competently use pellet pistols or firearms as per the Department’s Policy for Non\-Enforcement Personnel. Willing to handle live animals and carcasses, dispatch animals, and conduct simple tissue sampling and necropsies. Possess valid Driver's License and be able to safely and effectively operate watercraft and Utility Task Vehicles (UTV)s, as well as tow trailers. This job requires daily operation of State vehicles to reach field sites, regular use of kayaks, and occasional operation of UTVs and motorized watercraft. Must wear Department uniform.  

  

Be willing and able to obtain a California Boater Card and other motorboat operator certifications as determined necessary.  

  

The primary geographical focus of this position will be in San Joaquin, Sacramento, Contra Costa, Solano, Alameda, and Calaveras counties, but work may be assigned in any part of the area of nutria infestation.

We are an award\-winning California\-based environmental consulting firm with 550\+ professionals and more than 30 years of diverse experience serving clients in transportation, energy, water, infrastructure, private development, and government sectors. **About The Role**


Rincon Consultants, Inc. is seeking a **Principal or Director, Stormwater \& Watershed Sciences** to lead and grow our construction and industrial stormwater quality services throughout California.

Visit* *DEQ’s* *Civil Rights and Environmental Justice page**.*

**Are you passionate about preserving, enhancing, and protecting Oregon’s environment?** If so, please consider a career with the State of Oregon at the Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ). At DEQ, employees have the opportunity to work with a dynamic and supportive team of mission\-focused individuals tasked with maintaining, restoring, and enhancing the quality of Oregon’s air, land, and water.


The Oregon Department of Environmental Quality has a full\-time opportunity available for a **Drinking Water Protection Specialist (Natural Resource Specialist 3\)**. This position will be located in Portland, Oregon.


This is limited duration through June 30, 2027 with the potential of being extended and/or made permanent pending Budget and Legislature approval.


Please consider joining an innovative team, and work to advance our agency’s mission to protect and improve Oregon’s environmental quality.

**About DEQ!**


The Oregon Department of Environmental Quality is the primary regulatory agency of the government of the U.S. State of Oregon responsible for protecting and enhancing the state's natural resources.


The Water Quality Division has a critical role in achieving the Department’s mission by developing policy, implementation tools, and implementation priorities for improving and protecting the quality of water in Oregon’s waterways. The Water Quality Division works cooperatively with the Department’s three regional offices and the Laboratory to deliver programs and services that protect and enhance the quality of the waters of the state to protect public health and the environment.


The Standards, Source\-water Protection, and Assessment Section is responsible for the implementation of DEQ’s Drinking Water Protection Program for source water protection. The Section is also responsible for development and adoption by rule of water quality standards, identification of outstanding resource waters and water quality limited waters, conducting a statewide water quality assessment and assembling a biennial status report on Oregon’s water quality, and providing scientific and technical assistance to the regions, laboratory, and other water quality program sections on water quality standards.


For a visual representation of DEQ’s offices and their locations, view our DEQ Offices and Vehicle Inspection Testing Stations map.

**What you will do!**


You will work with DEQ and Oregon Health Authority staff in partnership to develop strategies under authority of the Clean Water Act to meet the goals and objectives of the 1996 Safe Drinking Water Act for drinking water source protection. In addition, you will provide outreach and technical assistance to Oregon’s public drinking water systems to identify sources of contamination and reduce pollution risks to their drinking water source areas.

**What’s in it for you!**


The opportunity to work in a productive and creative environment where no two days are ever the same! DEQ cares deeply about employee wellness and benefits. We offer a competitive benefits package that offers comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans for the employee and their qualified family members, as well as paid sick leave, vacation leave, personal leave, and 11 paid holidays a year. In addition, we offer membership in the Public Employees Retirement System (PERS), and you have the opportunity to potentially receive loan forgiveness under the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program (PSLF). If you are passionate about Oregon's environment, apply today!

 *This is a full\-time, AFSCME represented position.*

*This recruitment may be used to fill future vacancies.*

**What are we looking for?**


6 years of experience in a natural resource or environmental field, with at least 1 year of experience at a technical or professional level performing activities in a natural resource program such as researching and analyzing data, conducting investigations, applying pertinent laws and regulations, or coordinating and monitoring project activities.

* *Bachelor’s degree in physical science, environmental science, natural resources, or a closely related field may substitute for 3 of the required years of experience.*

The Office of Energy Infrastructure Safety’s Environmental Science Division is seeking an Environmental Scientist to analyze performance with vegetation management commitments in electrical utility Wildfire Mitigation Plans (WMP).

Work closely with internal teams to develop and present proposals, technical solutions, and service offerings.
Negotiate contracts and service agreements to align with client needs and financial objectives.
Provide industry insight and stay updated on environmental regulations, compliance standards, and emerging trends.
Support cross-business collaboration to provide integrated environmental solutions across multiple sectors.

About AECOM’s Environment Business Line

Join AECOM to be part of an expert global team who is connected through a well-developed, worldwide, internal technical practice network through which you can learn from and brainstorm with the best in the world. AECOM is an industry-leading, world class environmental firm, and we want you to succeed within it. We respect and encourage your own pathway to excellence via our Freedom to Grow initiative.

jobs.description:
**About Us**
============

At Onterris, we build careers grounded in purpose, responsibility and real\-world impact.


“For Planet and Progress” is our north star that guides everything we do. We believe environmental responsibility and human progress are interconnected, interwoven and international. Our scientists, engineers, field teams, consultants and professionals collaborate across disciplines and geographies, guiding industries and governments, ensuring that communities and environments thrive.


When you join us, you’re not just forging a career, you’re joining a movement. A movement for better thinking, smarter solutions and lasting impact.


Together, we will advance our way of life and protect the integrity of our environment every step of the way.


**A Day in the Life**
---------------------

Formerly known as Epic Environmental, the Australian arm of Onterris has kept the strong culture we are well known for. The team continues to work closely with clients, building trusted relationships and delivering high\-quality outcomes without an overemphasis on KPIs .


Our teams have the opportunity to work alongside industry leaders, auditors, and professionals with vast experience within our industry, while enjoying regular social events and collaborative work that bring the team together. Onterris also supports career development through relevant internal opportunities and individual one\-on\-one career conversations focused on growth and progression.  



We are seeking a n experienced Environmental Scientist to join our growing Contaminated Land and Water team out of our Brisbane office. Have the opportunity t o work alongside more than 45 land and water professionals across Australia who are actively invested in mentoring, collaboration and your long\-term career development.


This role will be responsible for a full range of activities including:


* Planning and delivering field investigations across a variety of sites – including soil, groundwater, and surface water assessments
* Preparing clear and high\-quality reports
* Acting as the representative/client contact on site for Onterris
* Attending business development meetings
* Supporting project managers and ensuring open and clear communications when in the field
* Project managing minor projects
**Your Expertise and Skills**
-----------------------------

These requirements reflect the knowledge, skills and abilities that help you do your best work here.


* 3\-5 years consulting experience in contaminated land
* Tertiary qualifications in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Management or related disciplines

Onterris is a leading global environmental solutions company partnering with organizations to solve complex challenges where environmental pressures, regulatory expectations and operational risks intersect. Guided by our mission to advance the way of life without compromising the integrity of our environment, we believe environmental responsibility and human progress are fundamentally connected. Our scientists, engineers, field teams and consultants apply systems thinking that unites science, data and practical expertise to deliver solutions that strengthen our clients’ resilience, mitigate risk and protect the air, water and soil that sustain communities, while uncovering responsible paths forward for planet and progress. Atoco, Inc. is a startup company founded by the distinguished scientist Prof. Omar Yaghi, the inventor of MOF and COF chemistry, for which he was awarded the Nobel Prize in 2025. Atoco is currently working on technologies in the fields of atmospheric water harvesting and CO₂ capture.
